keyChanges.title: Texas Cybercab roster jumps from 58 to 126 while rider-tagged cars stay near 44
keyChanges.description: Texas automated-vehicle records moved from 58 Cybercabs on September 21 (390 Model Y, 448 total) to 69 on September 22 (410 Model Y, 479 total), held at 69 Cybercabs through September 25, then added 57 Cybercab VINs on September 26 to reach 126, with Model Y unchanged at 420 and the combined Tesla Robotaxi authorization at 546. That September 26 step is a registry print, not a verified dispatch increase. The same day's community scrape tagged 44 Cybercabs in Austin (41 VIN-matched to the Texas roster, 409 logged trips), up by one from 43 the day before. Tesla's September 22 post that Cybercab #67 joined the Austin fleet landed on the day the roster stepped from 58 to 69 and is not a separate live-fleet census. Tesla Oracle described the 126 as operating. Paid Cybercab service is still Austin-only. Highway and at-grade rail detours were not shown as fixed, and NHTSA's sworn FMVSS answers are still due September 30.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Headlines treat the Texas DMV list as an operating fleet. Rider-tagged Cybercabs stayed near 44 when authorizations jumped by 57 in a day, and paid service is still Austin-only.

positive_signals: Authorized Texas Cybercab VINs rose from 58 on September 21 to 126 on September 26, including a same-day batch of 57.
Model Y listings on the same authorization stayed at 420 while Cybercab listings rose, so the new VINs are purpose-built cars rather than a relabel.
negative_signals: Community sightings tagged 44 Austin Cybercabs on September 26, only one more than September 25, against 126 registrations.
The Texas roster does not publish city, and a VIN listing is not a car giving a paid ride.
Tesla Oracle's operating-fleet framing treats the DMV list as live dispatch.
Paid Cybercab service remains Austin-only, with the September 30 NHTSA deadline still open and prior highway and rail detours unfixed.

key_metrics.actual: 126 Texas-authorized Cybercabs on Sept 26 (420 Model Y; 546 combined); about 44 rider-tagged in Austin
key_metrics.target: Paid Cybercab service outside Austin; NHTSA sworn answers due Sept 30
key_metrics.trajectory: Authorizations stepped up sharply this week; tagged riders did not

keyChanges.title: Robotaxi app 26.8.2 decompile shows Stop Now and door-unlock strings, not shipped features
keyChanges.description: Tracker Tesla App Updates decompiled Robotaxi iOS build 26.8.2, stamped September 21, 2026, and posted the strings on September 24. The build contains a geofenced SET_SUMMON_STOP_NOW_LATCH, a cellular door-unlock backup when Bluetooth or UWB fails, Cybercab door-tip images, cabin brightness controls, referral UI, and X Money wallet strings. The App Store changelog for the build is minor fixes and improvements. Tesla did not announce the features, and unused strings are not a rider-facing release. Cybercab booking itself is not new in this build; Austin riders have been able to request the car since the September 3-4 public opening. A Basenor writeup that treats 26.8.2 as the update that makes Cybercab bookable overstates a changelog that does not say that.

positive_signals: Stop Now and a cloud door unlock address real Cybercab gaps: no driver to flag and no conventional door handles.
TeslaNorth and Drive Tesla Canada describe the same September 24 decompile.
negative_signals: The public changelog is only minor fixes, and Tesla has not confirmed the strings are live.
X Money and referral UI are not shown in a Tesla release note.
Austin door and stop behavior is unchanged until the code ships to riders.

keyChanges.title: October 6 TCMV Agenda Has No Vote on EU-Wide FSD
keyChanges.description: The draft agenda for the 119th Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles meeting on 6 October 2026 does not schedule a vote on the Netherlands' Article 39 request to extend FSD Supervised across the EU. TeslaNorth, Teslarati and Electrek all report the only related item as 'continuation of discussions on request of the Netherlands for an Art. 39 authorisation,' slotted 11:45–12:10 (25 minutes). Tesla is not named, and none of the agenda items is a vote. Electrek says the DG GROW draft is dated 11 September, so the no-vote slot existed before this week's headlines. What is new in this window is that the 6 October vote Tesla Europe pointed to on 1 September is now publicly off the table. Elon Musk replied 'Sigh' on 25 September. Teslarati and Electrek say the next TCMV session is in December and treat that as the earliest a bloc-wide vote can happen. TeslaNorth is stricter: no later decision date is on an official schedule. The same committee has already discussed the file without voting, including at the 30 June meeting. Seven EU states — the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia and Czechia — have recognised the Dutch provisional approval. Teslarati and Electrek put those seven at about 53 million people, roughly 12 percent of the EU, against a qualified majority of 15 of 27 states representing 65 percent of the population (about 292 million). Electrek puts Germany, France, Italy and Spain at about 58 percent of EU population, so 65 percent stays out of reach unless at least one of those four votes yes. France has not recognised the approval. In July the transport minister said the system was not safe enough on speed and urban driver attention, and no UTAC result was published between 19 and 26 September. A discussion-only agenda does not revoke the seven national clearances. It is another slipped EU-wide date after a denied February Dutch target, a missed summer EU rollout, and a June meeting with no vote. The comitology PDF itself (CMTD(2026)1554) did not render on fetch; the agenda wording is from the three news reports.

positive_signals: The seven national recognitions stay in force; the agenda does not withdraw them
The Dutch Article 39 request is still on the 6 October agenda for discussion, not deleted
negative_signals: No vote is listed; the slot is 25 minutes of continued discussion
Tesla Europe had pointed to 6 October as a potential EU-wide vote; Musk's 25 September reply was 'Sigh'
This is another slip after February, summer and the June meeting produced no EU-wide authorisation
Seven states and about 12 percent of EU population versus a bar of 15 states and 65 percent
Germany, France, Italy and Spain still have not recognised the Dutch approval; France's July speed and driver-attention objections are unresolved and no French test result landed this week
Teslarati and Electrek put the next opening in December; TeslaNorth says no later decision date is scheduled

keyChanges.title: Czechia Recognises Dutch FSD Supervised Approval, Seventh EU State
keyChanges.description: On 21 September 2026 the Czech Ministry of Transport recognised the provisional EU type approval for Tesla FSD Supervised that Dutch authority RDW issued on 10 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) 2018/858 Article 39. The ministry said Czechia joins the Netherlands and five other European countries — seven in total — and that the system may be used in Czechia only on the conditions of that provisional approval. It is an SAE Level 2 assistance system: the driver must stay fully engaged and remains entirely responsible. Transport Minister Ivan Bednárik said safety was the priority and that the data convinced Prague to follow the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark and others. The release says officials examined speed-limit compliance, road signs, driver monitoring, speed offset and contextual speed, and that later documentation plus experience from states already using the system answered earlier objections. Prague had previously refused to recognise the Dutch approval automatically and preferred a coordinated EU decision. The ministry did not publish the technical file that changed its mind, and it set no activation date. Tesla Europe posted the same day that FSD Supervised is now approved in Czechia and that rollout will begin soon, with no date and no hardware or first-wave list. Reuters described the decision as a reversal of a sceptical stance on speed-limit compliance and driver oversight. This is mutual recognition of one existing provisional exemption, not a new Czech homologation and not an EU-wide authorisation. Teslarati and Electrek, writing after this clearance, put the seven states at about 53 million people, roughly 12 percent of the EU, still short of 15 states and 65 percent. Germany, France, Italy and Spain have not recognised the approval.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: A seventh national recognition is real, but it is the same provisional Dutch Article 39 file, still Level 2, with no activation date and no EU-wide vote.

positive_signals: Official Czech Ministry of Transport recognition on 21 September 2026 under Article 39
Tesla Europe confirmed approval the same day and said rollout will begin soon
Ministry says it reviewed speed limits, signs, driver monitoring and operating experience from states already using the system
Seventh EU member state to clear FSD Supervised for supervised use on public roads
negative_signals: Not an independent Czech type approval and not an EU-wide authorisation; it recognises the same provisional Dutch file
No activation date; 'soon' is not a rollout
Still SAE Level 2, with the driver fully responsible
Prague's earlier objections were speed compliance and driver monitoring; the evidence that resolved them was not published
Seven states and about 12 percent of EU population do not meet the 15-state and 65 percent qualified majority
The same week, the 6 October TCMV sitting was confirmed as discussion only, so this clearance does not unlock the rest of the bloc

key_metrics.actual: 7 EU states recognising the Dutch provisional approval, about 12% of EU population
key_metrics.target: 15 of 27 states and 65% of population for a qualified majority
key_metrics.trajectory: Seventh recognition on Sept 21; the Oct 6 TCMV slot is discussion only

keyChanges.title: Brussels Safety Study Finds FSD Speeding in Most 30 km/h Segments
keyChanges.description: On 24 September 2026 Brussels pedestrian-and-cyclist group johanna.be published its FSD30 study of Tesla FSD Supervised on low-speed streets. The driving was in July, about 400 km over three days, not a new test this week. TeslaNorth and Electrek report that in the Brussels-Capital Region the car exceeded the legal limit on 55 percent of tested 30 km/h segments, at an average speed of 44 km/h when it did, and exceeded the 20 km/h home-zone limit in 42 percent of locations reviewed. The group says a pedestrian hit at 44 km/h faces nearly six times the death risk of one hit at 30 km/h, citing WHO figures. TeslaNorth also reports repeated attempts to pass cyclists on cycle streets, where Belgian law bans that manoeuvre, and a speed display that often showed 50 km/h in 30 km/h zones, including after the cameras had read a 30 km/h sign. Indexed text of the group's report says the runs were done with speed offset and contextual maximum speed disabled, and that the car still sped after detecting the limit — a different claim from Tesla's September dashboard argument that the system matches surrounding traffic. The same coverage says the car generally yielded to pedestrians and cyclists, and the group says that does not offset the speeding. The report was sent on 7 September to RDW and the Flemish mobility ministry with a request to reconsider the approvals. TeslaNorth says RDW received it and will consider it in monitoring; that reply is not in the group's own publication note. This is one advocacy organisation and one car, not a regulator test and not a withdrawal of the Belgian or Dutch approval. It documents the failure mode France and Sweden have already used to withhold EU-wide authorisation, inside a country that approved the system in June.

positive_signals: The group says FSD generally handled pedestrians and cyclists cautiously and often yielded
Belgium and the Netherlands have not withdrawn their approvals on the back of this study
negative_signals: 55 percent of tested Brussels 30 km/h segments over the limit, averaging 44 km/h on those segments
42 percent of reviewed home zones over the 20 km/h limit; repeated cycle-street passes where overtaking is banned
Speed display often showed 50 km/h in 30 km/h zones, including after a 30 km/h sign was detected
Indexed report says speeding occurred with speed offset and contextual max speed disabled, so this is not only Tesla's traffic-matching exemption
Sent to RDW and the Flemish ministry on 7 September asking them to reconsider approvals; speed compliance is the objection blocking France and Sweden
Single advocacy test of one car in July, published 24 September — not an official homologation failure or a recall

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.10 (2026.27.11) widens in North America on unchanged v14.3.9 notes
keyChanges.description: Firmware 2026.27.11, published September 23 by Not a Tesla App and first seen September 22 on Teslascope, carries the same FSD versions as the prior drip: v14.3.10 on HW4 and v14.2 Lite on HW3. Not a Tesla App states the FSD version is unchanged from 2026.27.10. The v14.3.10 bullets are still the v14.3.9 list, including the MLIR compiler claim and Automatic Collision Evasion, and the notes still place pothole avoidance and reasoning beyond destination handling under Upcoming Improvements. TeslaFi showed about 11.5% of its sample (1,438 cars) on 2026.27.11 while installs were still arriving. Teslascope's active-update table on September 26 put 2026.27.11 at 17.7% of tracked software in North America, with 2026.27.10 still at 1.7%. That firmware share is not FSD-version share: Teslascope's AI4 table lists v14.3.10 on 2026.27.11 at 3.2% and on 2026.27.10 at 1.1%, while v14.3.8 on 2026.26.6.5 is still listed at 6%. No v14.3.11, v14.4, or customer v15 build showed up in this window.

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.9 false camera-service alerts; Tesla Support calls it a software bug
keyChanges.description: Owners on FSD v14.3.9 (builds 2026.27.5 and 2026.27.6) are getting a center-screen warning, "Poor camera visibility detected. Interior windshield residue cleaning is required," on cars whose forward cameras are clean. Not a Tesla App, citing a Tesla Support reply posted by @CARN0N on September 20 plus matching owner reports, says Tesla has acknowledged a software bug, is canceling cleaning appointments, and is telling drivers not to book service for this alert. The same build added Automatic Collision Evasion. The follow-up, v14.3.10, reprints the v14.3.9 notes and does not mention the alert, so a fix is not documented. Not a Tesla App said reports of the false alert were still concentrated on v14.3.9 as v14.3.10 began to move. Drive Tesla Canada repeated the Support acknowledgment on September 22.

positive_signals: Tesla Support acknowledged a software bug and service is canceling visits, so this is not a failed camera
negative_signals: The shipping HW4 build prompts owners to service a clean windshield camera
The vision check is firing on ordinary glare, which raises attention warnings while FSD is engaged
v14.3.10 notes do not document a fix
Some owners already paid for interior-camera cleaning before the bug was identified

keyChanges.title: HW3 refresh Model S and Model X get first FSD v14.2 Lite installs
keyChanges.description: Not a Tesla App reported on September 23 that HW3 Model S and Model X have started receiving FSD v14.2 Lite for the first time, on firmware 2026.27.10 and 2026.27.11. HW3 Model 3 and Model Y have had a v14 Lite branch since late June. The new wave is small. Not a Tesla App says only redesigned S/X have been seen so far and legacy S/X are still waiting. TeslaNorth, citing a September 22 owner post, confirmed a Model S showing 2026.27.10 and called it the first v14 build for those flagships. The published 2026.27.11 release notes still list FSD v14.2 Lite models as Model 3 and Model Y only, so the S/X expansion is ahead of the model list in the notes. Lite remains a distilled HW4 v14 port. Automatic Collision Evasion stays HW4-only. This does not put v15 on HW3.

keyChanges.title: Fremont Optimus hit hundreds a week in August — internal V3 units that still cannot generalize
keyChanges.description: The Information reported on 25 September 2026 (Qianer Liu and Grace Kay; Tesla did not respond) that Fremont built several hundred Optimus robots a week in August, up from a few dozen a week in Q2 small-batch testing, on the former Model S and Model X line. Managers want a continuous automated line above 1,000 robots a week by year-end and an eventual pace near 20,000 a week. Those are capacity goals, not shipments. The machines are described as Optimus V3 — lighter, with more cameras and a more human-like body — but sources said this is not the version Tesla plans to commercialize. That version still has to meet tougher durability and reliability requirements. Most units are for internal testing, training, and data collection. Robots used in Tesla factories stay in controlled areas on specific programmed tasks, not general-purpose work and not teleoperation. Each hand-and-forearm still has more than 100 screws and other small parts that a worker assembles by hand. Fixtures for hands, joints, and electronics testing lose alignment when the line runs faster, so more robots need rework. Touch-sensor durability is poor enough that a replaceable sensing glove, meant to avoid swapping the whole hand, is planned for 2027 and is not on the robots being built now. Suppliers, many in China, can make acceptable motors and precision gears in prototype quantities and then miss that quality at volume. Tesla is qualifying additional suppliers and offering larger orders to place some of that work outside China. Three people familiar with the AI said Optimus cannot yet handle a wide range of tasks and can behave unpredictably outside its training data. Even a basic task can take days to learn. The publication cites more than 500,000 hours of training data and a goal to double that by year-end, collected with motion-capture suits and camera helmets at hubs in Colorado, Arizona, and Florida after some California and Texas factory workers objected to recording demos for machines built to replace them. The commercial path in the report is a lease, not a sale, to a short list of factories and warehouses that look like Tesla's. No signed lease or delivery date is named. Ars Technica, The Verge, Electrek, and Humanoids Daily all rest on that one account. It is not a Tesla IR number, and it does not repair the missed 2025 target of about 10,000 robots with several thousand doing useful work, or the Gen 3 reveal that was supposed to land by mid-2026 and still has not.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: The ramp headline is an unconfirmed Information account of internal V3 robots that still cannot generalize, with no customer shipment and no Tesla unit count.

positive_signals: August weekly output is described as roughly ten times the Q2 small-batch rate, several hundred units versus a few dozen, on the converted Fremont S/X line
Training set cited at more than 500,000 hours, with dedicated collection hubs after some factory workers refused to record replacement demos
A lease to similar factories and warehouses is a narrower commercial plan than an immediate public sale
negative_signals: Tesla did not comment. There is no IR unit count, no customer delivery, and no named lease
The V3 robots on the line are not the commercial version; durability and reliability bars are still unmet
AI does not generalize. Basic tasks can take days, and factory use is supervised and task-specific
Hands are still manual assemblies of 100-plus small parts; touch sensors are unreliable; the sensing-glove fix is described for 2027
Suppliers hold prototype quality and miss it at volume; faster line speed increases rework
The 2025 promise of about 10,000 units with several thousand doing useful work, and a mid-2026 Gen 3 reveal, are both still unmet

key_metrics.actual: Several hundred a week in August, per The Information; Tesla did not confirm
key_metrics.target: Reported manager aim above 1,000 a week by year-end; not a Tesla IR target
key_metrics.trajectory: Up from a few dozen a week in Q2 small-batch testing; still internal and non-generalizing

keyChanges.title: Gen 3 Optimus app images are August mock art, not a hardware reveal
keyChanges.description: Public posts on 22–23 September 2026 treated Tesla Android app images as an accidental Optimus Gen 3 reveal. WholeMars extracted side-by-side renders and then deleted the post; Tesla Newswire reshared them. Ming (@tslaming) said he verified robot_closeup_gen3.png, robot_home_full_body_gen3.png, and robot_home_inactive_gen3.png in app 4.60.5-4573 and cautioned that the art may not be the final production design. Teslarati called the look factory-ready and said the files were validated by Grok as official, which is not a hardware confirmation. Humanoids Daily opened build 4.61.0-4607 and matched nine robot PNGs byte for byte under assets/mock/, including three _gen3 files. Across four builds, the _gen3 set first appears on 27 August (4.60.0-4542), the full-body and inactive images jump from 402×355 to 1206×1065 on 5 September (4.60.5-4573), and the 22 September build is byte-identical to 5 September. The gen3 full-body image covers hips and lower legs that the paired gold image leaves exposed. That shows a more enclosed skin in the artwork only. It does not measure hands, payload, or a line-ready robot. JavaScript in those builds does not reference the robot filenames. The only _gen3 code string Humanoids Daily found is the Gen 3 Wall Connector. Tesla has not commented. There is still no Gen 3 unveil after the Q1 2026 date slipped and Musk later said the design would be held until closer to production.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: The images are real files in the Android app, but they have sat in assets/mock/ since August and Tesla has not shown hardware.

positive_signals: Public Android builds have carried explicitly named _gen3 robot artwork since 27 August 2026
The gen3 full-body render is more enclosed at the hips and lower legs than the gold variant in the same package
Ming and Humanoids Daily independently found the same three gen3 filenames in the signed app assets
negative_signals: The files sit in assets/mock/ and do not confirm final hardware, dexterity, or a working Optimus screen
They are not new this week: the 22 September build is byte-identical to 5 September
Tesla is silent, and the official Gen 3 unveil missed both the Q1 2026 window and the later mid-year window
Teslarati's factory-ready framing overclaims static PNGs

keyChanges.title: Sanhua and Joyson will not confirm Optimus supplier certification headlines
keyChanges.description: The Ningbo audit story already filed for 18 September escalated this week without a confirmation from the companies named. Teslarati on 20 September, citing a Bloomberg account via RobotAIGeek, said the 16–17 September visit moved Tuopu Group, Ningbo Joyson Electronic, and Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls from provisional status to certified mass-production partners, with supply-chain talk of an initial batch near 5,000 units and a near-term goal of about 1,000 Optimus a week by late September. The Paper, written up by CnEVPost on 21 September and repeated by TeslaNorth the same day, said audits also cover Hangzhou and Shanghai, that the suppliers had already received Optimus orders of different sizes, and that production would start soon after the lines pass quality and compliance checks. On 22 September Global Times said Tesla declined to comment. Sanhua and Joyson told Global Times they had no knowledge of the reported factory audits and declined to discuss Tesla cooperation, citing commercial confidentiality. Global Times did not reach Tuopu. Interim reports from the three firms do describe robotics, actuators, or a humanoid subsidiary as a growth bet. That is not a new inspection, a certified award, or a Tesla purchase order. The 5,000-unit batch and the 1,000-a-week goal remain unnamed supply-chain figures, not Tesla disclosures.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Certified-partner and 5,000-unit headlines ran ahead of the companies. Sanhua and Joyson told Global Times they had no knowledge of the audits, and Tesla did not comment.

positive_signals: The Paper's account, if it holds, would extend the audit beyond Ningbo to Hangzhou and Shanghai and says orders were already placed
Tuopu, Sanhua, and Joyson already sit in Tesla's auto supply chain and describe robotics work in their own interim reports
negative_signals: Sanhua and Joyson told Global Times on 22 September they had no knowledge of the audits
Tesla declined to comment, and Global Times did not reach Tuopu
The certified-partner upgrade and the roughly 5,000-unit batch trace to a Bloomberg citation via RobotAIGeek, not a Tesla or supplier filing
This is the same 16–17 September visit already followed by vendor non-confirmations; a louder headline does not create a confirmed order

keyChanges.title: Tesla inaugurates Nevada Semi factory without disclosing a build rate
keyChanges.description: On September 24 Tesla held a Semi rollout at its Sparks, Nevada plant and said the truck is in high-volume production. The factory is about 1.8 million square feet beside Gigafactory Nevada, designed for 50,000 trucks a year (about 1,000 a week), with Standard Range, Long Range, and European-spec trucks on one line. That figure is nameplate capacity. Tesla did not disclose weekly output, an official sticker price, or 2026 shipments. The first truck off this line was in April, so the event inaugurated a line already described as ramping, nine years after the 2017 reveal and seven years after the 2019 production promise. PepsiCo has run pilot trucks since late 2022; branded cabs at the event for PepsiCo, DHL, US Foods, and others are not proof of a new run-rate. Outside estimates still put 2026 deliveries at 5,000 to 15,000. TechCrunch put the longest-range version just under $300,000 before incentives, versus the $150,000–$180,000 Tesla advertised in 2017, and said charging is still a hurdle even when customers are free to take trucks. Automotive World says Tesla is aiming for more than 30 Semi stations and 200 megawatt posts by year-end. Europe customer deliveries remain late 2027. A company claim of pilot-fleet uptime above 98% in 2026 does not measure the new line.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Opening the Sparks plant is a real event. High-volume production is a nameplate claim: no weekly rate, no official price, and no 2026 shipment count.

positive_signals: Dedicated Semi factory is open and Tesla says customer deliveries of the production truck start now
Same line is tooled for Standard, Long Range, and European-spec trucks, with a stated 50,000-a-year design capacity
High diesel prices strengthen the cost-per-mile pitch if trucks actually arrive
negative_signals: No weekly build rate, no official price, and no 2026 delivery target at the event
Original production promise was 2019; the high-volume line's first truck was already in April, so this is a coming-out, not a new start
Outside estimates of 5,000–15,000 deliveries in 2026 are far below the 50,000 nameplate
Charging remains the constraint, and Europe deliveries are still not until late 2027
Quoted price near $300,000 is roughly double the 2017 advertisement

key_metrics.actual: Sparks factory inaugurated Sept 24; no disclosed weekly build rate or 2026 shipments
key_metrics.trajectory: Coming-out for a line whose first truck was already in April; outside 2026 estimates remain 5,000-15,000

keyChanges.title: ZET SCALE names Tesla primary for 2,500 electric trucks; Semi share undisclosed
keyChanges.description: On September 22 ZET SCALE, a shipper alliance run by Catalyst Mobility (formerly CALSTART) and the Smart Freight Centre, named Tesla the primary OEM for an initial 2,500 battery-electric Class 8 trucks. Tesla Semi's post said '2,500 Semis on order' and that the deal would double the US electric Class 8 fleet. The alliance paperwork is looser than that post. Kenworth, RIDE, and Volvo are secondary OEMs carriers can choose, and no public table splits the 2,500 by manufacturer. Transport Topics, citing a Catalyst Mobility spokeswoman, said all 2,500 will be delivered by Tesla within 18 months, with the first in Q4 2026, purchased by ZET Financial and leased to shippers and carriers including Microsoft and PepsiCo. Other coverage still treats 2,500 as the alliance total, not a Tesla-only firm order. Either reading is an order book, not trucks delivered. An 18-month lease program does not show that the Nevada line can run at its 50,000-a-year nameplate, and North America remains the only Semi market until late 2027.

positive_signals: Tesla won the primary slot in a competitive RFP scored on price, range, charging, and production capacity
A Catalyst spokeswoman told Transport Topics the full 2,500 are Tesla trucks, first units in Q4 2026, all inside 18 months
Shipper members include Microsoft and PepsiCo, so the demand is aggregated freight rather than a single pilot fleet
negative_signals: Tesla's '2,500 Semis' post conflicts with secondary OEMs (Kenworth, RIDE, Volvo) and no published unit split
ZET Financial buys the trucks and leases them; this is not a Q3 delivery and not cash volume this quarter

Europe is still closed for Semi deliveries until late 2027

key_metrics.actual: Primary OEM slot on a 2,500-truck alliance; Tesla's post says 2,500 Semis, the public split does not
key_metrics.target: Trucks delivered, not an order-book headline
key_metrics.trajectory: Order or lease program into 2028 if the 18-month reading holds; not Q3 deliveries

keyChanges.title: Tesla China extends Model 3/Y cash discounts through Oct 31 and trims the Model Y cut
keyChanges.description: On September 25 Tesla China replaced its quarter-end inventory incentive with a new offer for orders through October 31. Every Model 3 gets 5,000 yuan off the final payment. Select Model Y variants, including Model Y L, get 7,000 yuan; the Model Y Performance is excluded. Five-year interest-free financing, an 8,000 yuan paint credit, and a choice of charging benefits remain. Non-Performance Model 3 trims also keep an 8,000 yuan insurance subsidy. List prices stay 235,500 yuan for the Model 3 and 263,500 yuan for the Model Y. Promotional posters show 222,500 yuan and 256,500 yuan after the applicable discounts. The new final-payment cuts cannot be combined with the September 7 inventory deal, which required delivery by September 30 and took 10,000 yuan off the Model Y. Extending direct cash past quarter-end, even with a smaller Model Y cut, is a demand concession. CnEVPost ties the move to CPCA figures: August China retail was 50,047, down 12.43% year over year, a third straight monthly decline, with Model Y at 29,260, down 25.76%. Year-to-date China retail is 316,251, down 12.44%, while Shanghai exports of 331,443 are up 114.70% and now exceed domestic deliveries. The factory is not the constraint. Local demand is.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: A smaller Model Y cut is not a demand recovery. Cash support now runs past quarter-end after three straight declines in China retail.

positive_signals: Model Y cash cut was reduced from 10,000 yuan to 7,000 yuan rather than deepened
Sticker prices were not cut; the support is a final-payment incentive plus financing
Shanghai exports of 331,443 through August are up 114.70% and exceed China retail

keyChanges.title: UBS sees 470k Q3 deliveries, above a lowered consensus but below Q2 and down 5% YoY
keyChanges.description: UBS analyst Joseph Spak on September 25 estimated 470,000 third-quarter deliveries, about 4% above a Visible Alpha consensus he put at 454,000, and kept a Neutral rating and a $385 target. UBS said it does not yet have Tesla's company-compiled consensus and expects that sheet within about a week. Tesla IR still shows only the July 2 Q2 release and the June 26 consensus; there is no Q3 production and delivery print, and the quarter does not end until September 30. Against Tesla's own numbers, 470,000 is a decline: about 5.5% below Q3 2025's 497,099 tax-credit quarter, and about 2.1% below Q2 2026's official 480,126. Spak put buyside expectations at 460,000–480,000 after they rose in recent weeks, so 470,000 can clear a lowered bar and still be down quarter over quarter. The unpublished range under that bar is still wide. Goldman remains at 435,000 and Barclays at 475,000, both already filed, and Visible Alpha has slipped from 456,000 to 454,000. If 470,000 holds, nine-month deliveries would be about 1.31 million, which UBS says is 7.4% above the same span of 2025, so the year is not negative while this quarter is. The note's regional checks are soft: estimated US August sales of 40,816, down 26% year over year, and China August retail of 50,047, down 12.4%.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Clearing a lowered Visible Alpha bar is not growth. 470k is still under Q2's 480,126 and about 5% under Q3 2025, and it is not a Tesla print.

keyChanges.description: Tesla's Robotaxi account said on Sep 23 that the first Cybercab was built with in-house cathode material from 'the first cathode plant in the Americas.' Berlin is unchanged: 4680 cell capacity there is still Construction, with 18 GWh not due until H1 2027.

keyChanges.title: County calls Terafab exempt from Abbott data-center permit freeze; state has not
keyChanges.description: On Sep 21, 2026, Gov. Greg Abbott directed TCEQ to halt all permits sought by data centers until ERCOT completes its audit, and said no state agency is to move forward with regulatory approvals related to data center development until PUCT, ERCOT, and the Texas Water Development Board have the information they require. TCEQ external-relations director Ryan Vise said the agency has paused all air and water permits and other authorizations for construction or development of infrastructure directly supporting data centers. Reporting on that same order says the freeze reaches projects that generate their own power, which the earlier ERCOT interconnection pause had left alone, because an on-site gas plant still needs a state air permit. KBTX asked whether this covers SpaceX's Grimes County project. County Judge Joe Fauth said, 'As far as I know,' it does not, because Terafab is a chip-manufacturing operation. He also said the site will have a data center 'only to aid their particular business,' that he has not heard from the governor's office, and that the project cannot use groundwater and instead plans recycled Gibbons Creek surface water plus its own power, off the ERCOT grid. KBTX reported Terafab was originally pitched to the county as a data center. Abbott's office, asked whether the pause includes Grimes County projects, referred KBTX back to the press release and did not state an exemption. TCEQ and SpaceX did not comment. County leaders said construction is still moving and that permits are unaffected. That is the county's position, not a TCEQ determination, and no Terafab permit was reported withdrawn this week. KBTX labeled Oct 19 as TCEQ's audit report; the governor's order is a TCEQ compliance update by Oct 19, while ERCOT's planned report to the PUC is Dec 10, after the JETI agreements' Dec 1 full-construction start. The order does not carve out a chip fab that includes an on-site data center and its own power.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: The county judge's exemption is not a TCEQ or Abbott determination. The order has no chip-fab carve-out, and the project was pitched with an on-site data center and its own power.

positive_signals: Grimes County Judge Joe Fauth says the pause does not hit Terafab because he classifies it as chip manufacturing, with any on-site data center only supporting the fab.
No Terafab air or water permit was reported pulled this week, and county leaders say site work is still moving.
ERCOT said its data-center impact RFI is not being sent to entities that are not interconnecting a data center to the ERCOT grid.
negative_signals: Abbott's Sep 21 order halts permits sought by data centers and tells every state agency not to advance data-center approvals until the audit information is in; the press release has no chip-fab exemption.
TCEQ says it has paused all air and water permits for infrastructure directly supporting data centers, and the freeze is described as covering self-powered projects the earlier grid pause missed.
Fauth has not heard from the governor, Abbott's office would not say Grimes projects are exempt, and TCEQ and SpaceX did not comment.
The project was originally pitched to the county as a data center and will include an on-site data center plus its own power, the exact features the freeze is written around.
The JETI full-construction start is still Dec 1, and ERCOT's report to the PUC is dated Dec 10, so the audit window runs through the date the agreements treat as the start of construction.

keyChanges.title: Austin research-fab slab gets more concrete; Grimes production start still Dec. 1
keyChanges.description: On Sep 22, 2026, drone observer Joe Tegtmeyer posted footage of more concrete going onto the main slab of the joint SpaceX-Tesla Advanced Technology Chip Fab at Giga Texas, tying reinforced footings and supporting structures together. He called it one part of a multi-part process. He was explicit that this building is the North Campus research fab, the precursor Tesla said it broke ground on in April, not the Grimes County production plant about 100 miles east. He described the Austin building as about $3 billion, with limited operations toward the end of 2027 and output on the order of a few thousand wafers a month. Basenor rewrote the same footage under a headline that Terafab is taking shape as concrete pours begin, which folds the pilot into the production project. On Sep 23 he pointed viewers who asked about the Terafab site back to his Sep 11 Grimes video, not to a new Grimes flight. No Tesla or SpaceX statement this week confirmed the pour. Slab concrete on the pilot is visible progress. It is not a cleanroom, not tool installation, and it does not move the Grimes JETI construction-start date of Dec 1, 2026.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: More concrete on the Austin pilot slab is visible progress. It is not the Grimes production plant, and the JETI full start is still Dec 1.

positive_signals: Sep 22 footage shows additional concrete on the main slab of the Giga Texas research fab, continuing footing and rebar work already underway.
Tesla has already described the North Campus building as the precursor it broke ground on in April.
negative_signals: The pour is the ~$3 billion Austin pilot, which Tegtmeyer says is still a multi-part slab, with limited operations aimed at the end of 2027.
Basenor's 'Terafab takes shape' headline treats the pilot pour as the production fab.
The latest Grimes site video he cited on Sep 23 is the Sep 11 flight; this window added no new Grimes construction release.
JETI full-scale construction start for Grimes County remains Dec 1, 2026, and neither Tesla nor SpaceX confirmed the pour.

keyChanges.title: TERA-print served in Terafab name suit; answer due Oct. 9 with no ruling
keyChanges.description: The Western District of Texas docket in Tesla, Inc. v. TERA-print, LLC, No. 1:26-cv-02543, shows a return of service filed Sep 22, 2026. TERA-print was served on Sep 18 and its answer is due Oct 9. On Sep 21 and Sep 23 the court granted pro hac vice motions, including for Tesla counsel Andrei Iancu and SpaceX counsel Megan Bannigan. The docket through Sep 25 shows no answer, no counterclaim, no injunction, and no hearing on whether Terafab infringes TERA-print's TERA-FAB registration. Service puts the defendant on the clock. It does not decide the name, and it does not remove the cease-and-desist cloud over the Grimes plant or the Austin pilot. The Sep 15 complaint was already reported; this week's entries only move the case from filing to an answer deadline.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Service and an Oct 9 answer date are on the docket. There is no ruling, so the Terafab name is still contested.

positive_signals: Plaintiffs completed service and the court set a date-certain answer deadline of Oct 9, 2026.
negative_signals: No declaratory ruling, injunction, or answer appears on the docket; the Terafab name is still contested.
Sep 21-23 entries are counsel admissions, not a decision on the trademark.
Service does not authorize use of the name at the Grimes site or the Austin research fab.

keyChanges.description: AltIndex's live count of Tesla LinkedIn openings was 8,001 on Sept 26, 2026, up 109 (+1.4%) from the 7,892 reading on Sept 19. AltIndex calls the level a hiring acceleration and says it is up 33.4% versus three months ago, but the monthly-average table on the same page (August 5,026, July 3,332, June 4,641) is a different series from the live spot count, so that percentage is not a clean measure of AI or robotics hiring. No Optimus or Tesla AI engineering requisition had a verified first-post date inside Sept 19–26. Listings that looked new were refreshes of older reqs, including Optimus hardware-validation mechatronics (posted July 17, Simplify update Sept 21, req 276993) and AI Engineer, Embodied Intelligence, Optimus (req 249027, board date about Sept 14). Data Collection Operator, Optimus remains live in Doral (req 279361, Simplify update Sept 22) and San Diego (req 270213) as motion-capture labor, not a new engineering wave. The START Optimus Service Technician winter 2027 cohort (req 281634) was already public on Sept 18, before this window.
